The provided documents detail the technical specifications, optimization campaigns, and user documentation for **Strata**, a local Large Language Model (LLM) inference engine. The materials are divided into two primary categories: a deep-dive engineering specification for optimizing performance on Intel Arc GPUs, and general reference guides for users and AI agents installing and configuring the software.

**Intel Arc A770 Optimization Campaign**
The core technical document, `A770_SPEED_SPEC.md`, outlines a rigorous effort to achieve at least 20 tokens per second (tok/s) in decode throughput on an Intel Arc A770 GPU using the Strata SYCL engine. The target model is Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Coder IQ1_M. The campaign begins with a baseline of ~9–11 tok/s and systematically tests various optimization levers, including kernel tuning, memory management, and architectural changes.

Initial work packages focused on reliable event-based measurements and BF16 projection paths. Microbenchmarks revealed that the default BF16 projection kernels were not the bottleneck; alternative row-based kernels were significantly slower. Register allocation tuning (GRF 128/256) also yielded no improvements or regressions. The investigation then shifted to quantized expert kernels (IQ formats). Standalone benchmarks showed these kernels accounted for only a small fraction of the total decode time (~24 ms out of ~123 ms per window), disproving the hypothesis that GPU compute saturation was the limiting factor.

A critical finding emerged from GPU utilization monitoring (`gputop`): the A770 was mostly idle (averaging ~20% usage) during decode. Profiling confirmed that the bottleneck was not GPU compute, but rather **per-layer host-to-GPU synchronization latency** and the CPU expert pool handoff.
